sentence: This project builds tools that track and move mRNA inside neurons and studies how its placement affects axon growth and spinal muscular atrophy.
This project studies how low oxygen affects hematopoietic stem cells and builds a gene correction system to help restore their functions.
This project supports cancer research in basic science and engineering and works to turn its advances into technologies and treatments.
This project uses stem cells from patients with Brugada syndrome to study why arrhythmias arise in the right ventricle and to test a treatment.
This project studies how genetic changes during a person's life affect immune cells in the brain and contribute to Alzheimer's disease.
This project supports radiology research that uses advances in imaging technology and methodology.
This project studies how HIV-1 enters a host cell and how entry inhibition works.
This project studies which signals in the adult intestine turn glial cells into neurons, including the role of macrophages and inflammatory cytokines.
This project tests whether two kinases help drive retinal ganglion cell death after axon injury, using rodent and human cell models.
This project uses single-cell RNA sequencing and computer methods to find existing compounds that might treat dermatomyositis.
This project uses single cell technologies to study how cancer cells and nearby immune cells change together during therapy.
This project tests a deep learning platform to see whether it can diagnose isolated dystonia in clinical studies.
This project builds tools to find out how choline transport and heme handling in cells link to congenital hydrocephalus.
This project uses transgenic mouse technology and single-cell epigenomics to study how noncoding variants in enhancers disrupt limb development.
This project uses brain imaging, including MRI, to study frontotemporal dementia and track how the disease changes over time.
This project studies how T cells and lymph nodes near tumors fight renal cell carcinoma, using human and mouse models.
This project studies how astrocytes drive multiple sclerosis and how they might be targeted by treatments, using animal models and clinical samples.
This project uses synthetic biology to control cell signals and build a layered arterial tissue, to learn how cells make decisions.
This project tests whether skin surface lipids collected with tape stripping can show if youth have non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and how severe it is.
This project develops a noninvasive imaging method that detects abnormal T cell activity in patients with Alzheimer disease.
